answer: The opal assignment is published and velvet records each panel. Shards are assigned from the cipher graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The grading quorum of 6 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an attacker cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 4113 identities would post 3083 proofs and burn roughly 64 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
